So I was urged to give DE shaving one last shot.

I got a Weish DE Razor and Derby blades (both recommended for sensitive skin) and found it gives a less bad experience than what I was used to.

It is less irritating than a cheap 2 blade disposable, but not quite as good as a dorco 3 blade.

For the price though it gives an acceptable shave, being able to change blades daily for $0.50 per week is nice.

The shave is also noticeably closer than with a cartridge.

Overall it's not horrible, I'm still on the fence as to if the savings balances out the extra irritation or not, but it's not as bad as my previous DE experiences which is a plus.
My apologies on DE safety razors

The only problem I've found with using a safety razor is with getting close under my nose. The head of the razor seems to cause a little bit of an issue with this. I also have an easier time getting real close on a shaped beard line with a regular bic razor than with a safety razor. The slightest miscalculation and I'm screwing up the line where as with a bic this doesn't happen with just a light touch. So usually I use a single blade bic for those two things.
I had far better luck with Gilette Silver Blue blades than anything else.

Before I started growing a beard, I used a disposable straight razor with Shark blades and Hawleywood's Liquid Cream Shave. I have sensitive skin and didn't have much of a problem if I properly lathered and didn't fuck up my technique. You sure it's the razor and not your lather? Either how much you're using, or the brand/style of lather you use?
Yes I am sure it is not the lather. I have tried traditional shaving gels, and brush made lather, and found that grapseed oil works a lot better and causes a lot less skin irritation.

This is 100% your technique, not the blades. Granted, maybe the razors just aren't for you; not everyone has the time/inclination to learn to use DE blades (I know I personally just don't want to bother with straights).

What I'm saying is if that it will get better, if you keep working on your technique, so don't write it off just because it doesn't work like a cartridge razor the first few times. That's like giving up on the violin because it doesn't sound as good as a recorder.
